findings.title: About twenty test fixtures pass `setting_sources=None` into a field the slice makes non-optional
findings.description:
`ReviewTemplate.setting_sources` is now `list[str]` with a "Never None" comment. Only the YAML loader enforces that: `_resolve_setting_sources` runs in `load_template`, and the dataclass (lines 26-27) has no `__post_init__`. Tests still build templates with `setting_sources=None`, for example `tests/review/test_review_client.py:35`, `tests/review/test_templates.py:186`, and `tests/review/test_rules.py:184`.

Production has no `None` path today, but nothing stops one. `review_client.py:220-224` passes the template value straight through. A `None` there drops the flag, so the CLI loads user settings, which is the outcome this slice exists to prevent. The artifact would show "cli default", so the problem is visible but not prevented. `pyproject.toml:94` sets pyright to `include = ["src"]`, so none of these fixtures are type-checked. Fix: add a `__post_init__` that rejects `None`, and update the fixtures to pass `["project"]`.

findings.title: `pipeline.background_idle_timeout_s` accepts `true`, `0`, and negative values
findings.description: The int branch of `get_typed_config` checks `isinstance(value, int)`, which is true for `bool`. The bool branch above it has a "bool before int" comment, but the int branch does not exclude bool. A hand-edited `pipeline.background_idle_timeout_s = true` returns `True`, which becomes a one-second idle bound. Zero or negative values also pass, and they make the timer fire at once, so every background agent is stopped immediately. The CLI path cannot produce a bool (`_coerce_value` calls `int()`), but hand-edited TOML can. `tests/config/test_keys.py` (`TestPipelineConfigKeys`) only covers the `"60"` coercion. Fix: reject bool explicitly in the int branch, require a positive value, and add tests for `true`, `0`, and `-1`.

findings.title: Synchronous config reads run on the event loop inside async functions
findings.description:
The project rule for async code says any `async def` that calls synchronous code must guarantee under 1 ms worst case, and reviewers must verify this. This slice adds `get_typed_config` calls in `one_shot_dispatch_with_telemetry` (`dispatch.py:147` and `:153`), in `open_pipeline_session` (`sdk_session.py:455-460`), and in `_collect_turns` through `_background_idle_timeout_s` (`sdk_session.py:224` and `:327`). Each call goes through `load_config`, which opens and parses two TOML files synchronously. `user_config_path()` can also run `shutil.copytree` during the one-time config migration. A file read cannot be guaranteed under 1 ms. One one-shot dispatch performs two full config loads on the loop.

Fix: read the three values once in a synchronous setup step (for example when the session is built), or move the read to `asyncio.to_thread`. I did not check whether the existing callers, such as `events/dispatcher.py:92` and `tools/cf_tools.py:221`, run in async functions. If they do, this is a pattern the slice follows, not one it introduces.

findings.title: No load test covers the new background-wait path
findings.description: `tests/load/` exists (`test_grep_timeout.py`, `test_worktree_concurrency.py`), and the project rule requires at least one load test for code on network or concurrency paths, asserting on latency, throughput, or resource bounds. `_collect_turns` adds a per-message idle timer, a ledger of concurrent background agents, and a stop fan-out. Every new test runs in-process against `ScriptedClient` with sleeps of 0.05 to 0.15 s, so none of them measures a bound. The slice doc does not mention a load test. Whether this path counts as network or concurrency is a judgment call, and I would treat it as one. Fix: add a load test that drives many background agents through `dispatch()` and asserts both the wall-clock bound and that the idle stop fires within the configured window.

findings.title: `sdk_session.py` is 472 lines
findings.description: The project guide asks for source files around 300 lines where practical. The slice split `sdk_turns.py` out "for size", but the remaining module still holds the client lifecycle, rotation and seeding, rate-limit retry, the background wait and stop loop, and the pipeline session builder. The wait machinery (`_collect_turns`, `_read_turn_with_retry`, `_read_turn`, `_background_idle_timeout_s`, `_stop_background`) is about 130 lines and is the obvious next extraction. It needs only the client, so it can move to `sdk_turns.py` or a sibling module without a new dependency.

findings.title: `_stop_background` catches bare `Exception` without re-raising
findings.description: Each failure is logged at ERROR with its traceback, and the loop continues to the next id, so nothing is silent. The project rule for `try/except`, though, is either to re-raise after logging or to catch a specific type with a justification. This does neither, and `# noqa: BLE001` suppresses the ruff check that would flag it. The in-code comment explains the SDK raises bare `Exception`, and the earlier review doc (932-review, F003) accepted the design. The code and the rule still disagree. Either record this as an explicit exception to the rule, or collect the failures and raise one aggregate error after the loop.

findings.title: The settings module docstring says no automated path leaves `setting_sources` unset, but `sq serve` does
findings.description: `ClaudeSDKProvider.create_agent` skips `setting_sources` when it is `None` (`provider.py:89-90`), and `describe_setting_sources` has a `cli default` branch for that case (`core/models.py:110-111`). The slice doc (line 47) explicitly excludes `sq serve` as "neither an automated pipeline or review path", so the code follows the design, but the docstring overstates it. Name the exception in the docstring.

findings.title: `base_env` is never used in production
findings.description: `kwargs` never holds an `env` key before line 86, so `base_env=kwargs.get("env")` is always `None`. The parameter exists for a future env source that does not exist yet, and passing it needs a `# type: ignore[arg-type]`. `test_base_env_keys_survive_and_input_is_not_mutated` exercises a path nothing calls. Remove the parameter, or keep it and drop the cast.

findings.title: The pipeline settings policy is read in two places
findings.description: `one_shot_dispatch_with_telemetry` and `open_pipeline_session` (`sdk_session.py:455-460`) each read `pipeline.user_settings` and `pipeline.auto_memory` and derive the sources and auto-memory flag. The policy was centralized in `settings.py`, but the key reads were not. A helper such as `pipeline_settings(cwd)` in `settings.py` would keep the policy in one place.

findings.title: The summary one-shot sends an empty system prompt on the SDK
findings.description: The config sets `instructions=""` and leaves `use_default_system_prompt` False, so the provider sends `--system-prompt ""` (`provider.py:63-64`). The dispatch comment at `dispatch.py:134-138` says an empty prompt on the SDK strips the CLI's tool-use discipline. The new record shows this path as `empty` (`summary_oneshot.py:136`, and the matching test in `test_summary_oneshot.py`). This predates the slice, but the recording makes the inconsistency visible. It needs a follow-up decision.

findings.title: A missing dispatch response is rendered as "(empty response)"
findings.description: `context.result.outputs.get("response", "")` falls back silently. Every dispatch success path sets `response`, so the default is unreachable today. If it ever fires, the flag reads as though the agent said nothing, which is a placeholder that looks like real output. Prefer an explicit marker such as "(no response recorded)".

findings.title: Loose typing hides errors at the new boundaries
findings.description:
Three cases:
- `sdk_session.py:466` suppresses `reportArgumentType` on `setting_sources`. That means `SdkSettings.setting_sources: list[str]` does not match what `ClaudeAgentOptions` expects. I could not check the SDK's declared type, so I cannot say which side is wrong. Typing the field with the SDK's own alias would make the contract explicit.
- `BackgroundLedger.observe` and `DispatchTurns.collect` take `msg: object` (`sdk_turns.py:55`, `:106`), so the type checker cannot check the message types they branch on.
- In tests, `scripted_session`, `sdk_text`, `sdk_result`, `typed_config`, and `failing_reconnect_patch` in `tests/pipeline/conftest.py` return `object`. That forces `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` at many call sites in `test_sdk_session.py`. Pyright does not check tests, so these hide errors without failing CI.

findings.title: `WAITED_TASK_TYPES` copies an SDK private constant
findings.description: The set `{"local_agent", "local_workflow"}` is copied from the SDK's private `DEFERRING_TASK_TYPES`, as the comment says. `pyproject.toml:29` pins only `claude-agent-sdk>=0.2.160` with no upper bound. If a later SDK adds a deferred type, dispatch would return before that work finished, and its follow-up would land in the next dispatch's discard path. Add a test that compares this set with the SDK's constant, so an SDK upgrade fails loudly.

structured_findings.summary: About twenty test fixtures pass `setting_sources=None` into a field the slice makes non-optional
Synchronous config reads run on the event loop inside async functions
No load test covers the new background-wait path
The settings module docstring says no automated path leaves `setting_sources` unset, but `sq serve` does
The pipeline settings policy is read in two places
The summary one-shot sends an empty system prompt on the SDK
A missing dispatch response is rendered as "(empty response)"
Loose typing hides errors at the new boundaries
